version.changelog: Failed tool calls are isError MCP frames (all transports); content unchanged.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper that stores sensitive local audit logs, but I found no hidden or malicious behavior in the inspected artifacts.

dimensions.detail: It reads limited agent-identifying environment variable presence, stores local SQLite audit data under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME, and says it makes no network connections; this is proportionate but audit logs may contain sensitive operational data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a uv package and Bash-based CLI examples. This is disclosed, versioned in the docs, and not accompanied by hidden download or execution instructions in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill auto-loads across the VMware skill family and wraps tool calls through a decorator, which is broad but clearly disclosed and directly tied to audit and policy enforcement.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit, rules, and undo databases are expected for this purpose and disclosed. No cron, service, startup hook, or cross-session backdoor behavior was found; policy bypass via VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED is disclosed as an operator escape hatch.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is shared audit logging, optional policy checks, and sanitization for VMware skills; the documented capabilities match that purpose and the skill exposes no MCP tools of its own.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want a shared VMware audit and policy layer. Configure ~/.vmware/rules.yaml before relying on it to block risky actions, protect audit.db and rotated archives as confidential, and restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED or modify the MCP host environment.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The credential-related terms appear in redaction documentation for parameters and results, not as instructions to read credential files.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad auto-loading is real, but it is disclosed as the shared infrastructure layer for VMware skills and is purpose-aligned.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set private permissions on ~/.vmware and audit.db; no sudo or root escalation was found.
[RA2] expected: The persistent files are local audit, rules, and undo state required for the feature, not unauthorized persistence.
[EA2] expected: The default policy denies nothing unless the user configures rules, but the artifact states this clearly and points users to RBAC, rules.yaml, and vmware-pilot for approval workflows.
[E3] expected: The filesystem command is a troubleshooting check for a specific rules file under ~/.vmware, not broad filesystem enumeration.
